chapter: The district underworld and street musicians
title: Lewis Wade, Paul Gross and Buddy Bertrand around the Big 25
summary: Dawson describes Lewis Wade as a pimp and pianist, Paul Gross as a gambler, and knowing pianist Buddy Bertrand only from the Big 25 district.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: You missed your chance. You could have had another one. Well, what about Lewis Wade, did you know that?
Lewis Wade, he was another swim, what you call a pimp around that district. Yeah, he was a big time. Now, what about the piano player? Well, he played piano and he was good.
And his brother Clark or Clark or whatever you want to call him?

Yeah, he was a gamble, that's all he did was play piano and gamble and have, you know, just like Paul Gross. Paul Gross, you heard of him. He got a ballroom out there on, gamble and a room and I think it is. Yeah. Did he play music? No, he didn't play no music but he was hustling around, he gambled, you know.
You knew Buddy Gara and Bertie Bertrand and all of them?
Bertrand and all of them, yeah. Old Dr. Weeks, you know, one-legged Dr. Weeks, all that bunch of them. I didn't know him. Felix King.
George, uh, Morris Moe. I've heard of him. Yeah, he was a fella about my car. Buddy Bertrand played over on the, uh, the piano around there. He was my, he was part of my car, yeah.
Did you hear Buddy Bertrand play music of him?
You just knew him in the, in the 25? Yeah. I met him in the 25.
Yeah, round that district down there.
